Puerto Rico, Canada and Mexico on AT&T/T-Mobile and Movistar/Telcel; Vyncs: AT&T/T-Mobile, Telus/Bell, Telefonica/Telcel; Spytec Pulse OBD: US, CA, MX) or what each maker offers when the vehicle has no usable OBD-II port (Vyncs' 12V adapter cable is GPS-only with no fault codes or fuel data; Spytec's optional splitter may block vehicle data; Bouncie can't be plugged into some Teslas).
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages (rottenwifi.com, vyncs.com/pricing.aspx, bouncie.com/pricing) and four uncited results (allinsider.net, gpstrackerreviews.net, tagandtether.com, hotairtag.com). Rottenwifi gives only 'most vehicles from model year 1996 onward' for Bouncie and 'nationwide U.S. coverage and international operation' for Spytec, with no countries or carriers. The Vyncs pricing page names no carrier or country list, and the Bouncie pricing page says only 'OBD2 | Telematics | GPS | 4G LTE'. Allinsider says Bouncie 'service is US-only' and gpstrackerreviews says 'Continental US coverage'; Bouncie's own FAQ contradicts both. No page read mentions Vyncs' 12V adapter cable, Spytec's splitter caveat, or the Tesla port exclusion. Not read: winchinsider.com (certificate error), konnectgps.com, autoskyus.com, safewise.com, roadandtrack.com, so the score is 2 rather than 3.
decides: For a US passenger car from 1996 on, all three plug in, so compatibility confirms the pick rather than changing it. All three also cover the US, Canada and Mexico, so border driving does not rule out Bouncie, despite what two rival pages say. The pick shifts in three cases. For a heavy-duty truck or bus without OBD-II, Vyncs is the only one of the three with a maker-documented 12V adapter cable, but it drops to GPS-only; Spytec's own answer for that case is its Pulse Hardwired tracker (8V to 32V DC). If the OBD port must stay free for another device, Spytec sells a splitter but warns it may stop the tracker reading vehicle data. If an alert on unplugging matters, Vyncs states it has no battery and cannot notify until power returns, while the Spytec Pulse OBD lists a 60 mAh backup battery.

findings.label: Countries supported
findings.value: United States (including Puerto Rico), Canada and Mexico
findings.source_title: Bouncie FAQs (Bouncie Help Center, dated February 24, 2026)
findings.note: Maker FAQ: 'Bouncie supports International use in United States (US, including Puerto Rico), Canada, and Mexico.' Contradicts allinsider.net ('service is US-only') and gpstrackerreviews.net ('Continental US coverage').

findings.label: Cellular carriers
findings.value: AT&T and T-Mobile 4G in the US; Movistar and Telcel in Mexico; internal SIM, no Wi-Fi
findings.source_title: Bouncie FAQs (Bouncie Help Center, dated February 24, 2026)
findings.note: Maker FAQ: 'Bouncie uses the AT&T and T-Mobile 4G Data Network.' The FAQ as read names no Canadian carrier.

findings.label: Electric vehicles and the Tesla exclusion
findings.value: Works in EVs that have an OBD2 port; cannot be plugged into the Tesla models that lack one
findings.source_title: Bouncie FAQs (Bouncie Help Center, dated February 24, 2026)
findings.note: Q 'Does Bouncie work in electric vehicles?' A 'The short answer is yes.' Without an OBD2 port, which the FAQ says some Tesla models lack, 'Bouncie can't be plugged in.'

findings.label: Vehicle requirement
findings.value: Any vehicle with an OBD2 port; passenger vehicles made after 1996 should have one; third-party adapters can convert another port to OBD2
findings.source_title: Compatible Vehicles (Bouncie Help Center, dated September 9, 2025)
findings.note: Article says Bouncie 'works with all types of vehicles' with an OBD2 port and that an unlisted model or year can still work if it has one. It names no specific adapter.

findings.label: Behaviour when parked
findings.value: Low-power mode that monitors the vehicle battery and checks in periodically
findings.source_title: Bouncie FAQs (Bouncie Help Center, dated February 24, 2026)
findings.note: 'Bouncie enters into a low-power mode where it monitors the health of the vehicle's battery.'

findings.label: Carriers in North America
findings.value: USA: AT&T, T-Mobile; Alaska: AT&T; USA regional: Viaero; Canada: Telus, Bell; Mexico: Telefonica, Telcel; Puerto Rico: AT&T, T-Mobile
findings.note: For locations outside the US, Canada and Mexico the page says to 'contact us regarding what device you should purchase', so the device sold in the US is documented for those three countries plus Puerto Rico.

findings.label: Vehicles without OBD-II (heavy-duty trucks, buses)
findings.value: 12V adapter cable gives GPS tracking, accelerometer-based unsafe-driving notifications and speeding alerts only; no fault codes, no fuel consumption data
findings.note: 'Heavy-duty vehicles usually do not have the OBD-II port.' 'The 12V adapter cable will provide you access only to GPS tracking features.' 'You will not receive fault codes and fuel consumption data.'

findings.label: Vehicle requirement
findings.value: OBD-II port, required by law on vehicles built and sold in the USA after 1996; in Europe, EOBD on petrol vehicles
findings.note: 'All vehicles built and sold in USA after 1996 must have an OBD-II port by law.' The FAQ as read does not address EVs, hybrids or diesel.

findings.label: Unplug alert and engine-off reporting

findings.note: 'The device does not have a battery for safety reasons.' It 'is not able to notify you until it regains power.' 'Even when the engine is off, Vyncs will update its location every hour.'

findings.note: Same page claims 'Worldwide coverage in 200+ countries' and 'Ultra-fast 4G LTE Device'.
